title: PRD — OneRoute hosted inference surface: contract, SLOs, and launch playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: This document defines the minimal operational surface and launch readiness plan for 'OneRoute', a single hosted inference adapter that consolidates chat/completions, embeddings, and rerank into a consistent API contract for customers. The goal is to ship a tight MVP that preserves behavioral guarantees for existing surfaces while simplifying onboarding and observability for hosted customers.
background: Multiple hosted endpoints (chat, generative completions, embeddings, rerank) currently have overlapping operational workstreams and inconsistent telemetry. OneRoute aims to provide a single adapter layer that maps client intents to optimized model variants and runtime policies, reducing cognitive load for PM/SE customers and enabling unified QoS controls.
goals: Provide a single, backwards-compatible route for common generation, embedding, and rerank requests
Define clear contractual semantics (input, output, errors) and compatibility guarantees for the first GA customers
Ship monitoring and rollout controls (canary, graded fallback) to meet SLOs for p99 latency and availability
Minimize per-token unit cost by enabling model variant routing and transparent batching settings
out_of_scope: Full multi-modal input (images/audio) — will be scoped to text-only for MVP
On-prem/VPC private control plane deployment — OneRoute MVP targets hosted infra only
End-user billing model changes — billing remains per-token and per-embedding unit
requirements: Functional: Single POST endpoint /v1/oneroute with a 'mode' field: 'chat' | 'generate' | 'embed' | 'rerank'
Functional: Mode-specific payload validation and structured output support (e.g., messages for chat, prompt for generation, vectors for embeddings, pair-list for rerank)
Functional: Streaming responses for generation and chat using same SSE/HTTP streaming contract
Non-functional: 99.9% availability for GA customers; p95 latency targets for small requests < 150ms for embeddings, < 400ms for generative text on standard models
Operational: Per-request tracing headers, token-level cost attribution, and route-level dashboards in Console
Safety: Input/response sanitization and configurable behavioral guardrails; admin-level controls to disable risky model variants
api_contracts: POST /v1/oneroute — body contains 'mode' and mode-specific fields. Response object includes 'request_id', 'model_used', 'duration_ms' and mode-specific result fields.
Streaming: SSE messages use event types 'chunk' and 'done'; each chunk contains 'delta' and 'cursor' fields. Consumers can reassemble streaming to match existing chat semantics.
Backward compatibility: Provide a compatibility shim for v1/chat and v1/completions for 3 months after launch to avoid client breakage
security: All requests must authorize using existing API keys; OneRoute respects per-key rate and quota limits
Support for region-based routing and DLP controls; model selection will be logged for audit
KMS-backed logs for enterprise customers enabled via feature flag
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal usage only — 2 weeks — smoke tests, heavy-load simulation against synthetic traffic
Beta: Opt-in customers plus internal devs — 3 weeks — collect telemetry, run gradated fallbacks and measure cost delta
Canary: 1% of production traffic for 48 hours with active monitoring and automatic rollback triggers
GA: Cross-check acceptance criteria, complete security review, publish docs and SDK updates, then open to all customers
Fallback plan: Automatic routing to pre-existing endpoint variants if OneRoute fails model binding or backend capacity
launch_checklist: API contract published with examples and migration guide in Developer Docs
Console dashboards created: per-route latency, cost-per-token, error-rate, model-variant distribution
SDKs updated (JS, Python, Go) with OneRoute helper functions and examples
Load and chaos test runbooks completed and results archived
Support playbook and escalation ladder published in PagerDuty runbook
Billing verification for token attribution and embedding unit counting
Legal & compliance signoff for data retention and audit logging for enterprise lanes
Security review completed and penetration-testing notes resolved
Canary automation scripts validated and rollback verified
Customer communications drafted: migration timeline, opt-in beta instructions, known limitations
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral parity: For mapped requests, output shapes and core semantics match existing endpoints within defined regression thresholds
SLOs: For GA customers the platform meets 99.9% availability and latency targets measured over a 7-day window
Observability: All OneRoute requests surface token-level cost and model selection in Console; alerts exist for error rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes
Rollback: Canary traffic can be fully migrated away within 15 minutes using automated scripts
Security: KMS integration tests pass for enterprise customers and audit logs are available for 90 days
SDK: Examples run end-to-end in CI and shipping SDKs include OneRoute helpers

notes: Trade-off: A single adapter simplifies developer experience but concentrates risk; mitigations include graded fallbacks and independent model pools per tier
Performance note: Embeddings must bypass certain batching heuristics to meet tight p95 latency; will expose 'fast_path' hint in request payload
Migration note: We propose a 3-month compatibility window for existing endpoints, with automated deprecation notices and opt-in flags
